story_body: The Kaduna State Government has begun revitalising 82 Primary Healthcare Centres across the state, with the intervention focused on upgrading facilities to Level 2 status and strengthening selected centres as Centres of Excellence.

The Kaduna State government publication said the intervention forms part of wider health-sector investments, with the stated objective of improving access, service utilisation, patient experience and health outcomes across communities.

The 11 facilities identified include Umaru Musa Yar'Adua University, Hassan Usman Katsina Polytechnic, three waterworks and a booster station, General Amadi Rimi Hospital, Turai Yaradua Maternity Hospital, the State House of Assembly and the State High Court.

The Special Adviser on Power and Energy said an assessment showed the facilities account for 93.4 per cent of the state government's total electricity expenditure. The approved intervention has a stated total capacity of 20 megawatts.

The government projects that the solar intervention could save about ₦7 billion and estimates that avoided expenditure on grid electricity and diesel generators could equal the investment within approximately three and a half years.

The state also reported that generation capacity had risen from zero megawatts when the current administration assumed office to more than 30 megawatts, with a target of 70 megawatts by 2031 under an Integrated Resource Plan developed with Power Africa.

newsReports.lead_narrative: Abia State hosted the 2026 World Igbo Day celebration in Umuahia, where Governor Alex Otti and other Igbo leaders addressed questions of unity, cultural continuity, education, enterprise and collective development.

story_body: Governor Alex Otti addressed the World Igbo Day celebration on September 29, 2026, under the theme 'Ohaneze: History and the Dreams of Tomorrow.' He called for collective interests to be placed above individual differences while acknowledging that unity does not require uniformity of opinion.

Otti identified education, apprenticeship and the traditional Omugwo system as channels through which knowledge, skills and values can be transferred across generations. He also urged cooperation and peaceful engagement among Ndigbo.

The celebration concluded with a wreath-laying ceremony at the Aguiyi Ironsi Cenotaph in honour of late eminent Igbo personalities. The event attracted political, traditional, religious and community stakeholders from across the Igbo community.

newsReports.title: BYM Demands Revocation of Plateau Mining Lease ML-129, Threatens Peaceful Protest

featured_image.aria_label: Plateau State Governor Caleb Muftwang Governance Policy Intelligence

newsReports.lead_narrative: The Berom Youth Molders-Association has called for the immediate revocation of Mining Lease No. ML-129 over a mining site in Latya, Du District of Jos South Local Government Area, Plateau State, while giving the Federal and Plateau State governments one week to respond to its demands.
newsReports.editorial_notice: This News Report provides qualitative subnational coverage. Developing events in this narrative maintain visibility across tracked jurisdictions and do not alter current Policy Signal Index (PSI) standings.
story_body: The association made the demand on Wednesday, September 30, 2026, during a press conference at the Nigeria Union of Journalists Secretariat in Jos. Its president, Dalyop Solomon Mwantiri, said the association's concerns centred on what it described as alleged irregularities surrounding the issuance and operation of ML-129, while acknowledging that mineral resources are vested in the Federal Government.

According to the association, unresolved issues also surround an earlier Mining Lease No. ML-126, which it said was associated with Mining Technologies Company Limited and covered the disputed area. The BYM alleged that an agreement connected with the earlier mining operation was for four years and expired in 2001, while legal proceedings concerning ML-126 remained pending before the High Court and the Court of Appeal in Jos.

The association further alleged that Mr. Joshua Egbagbe subsequently obtained ML-129 while the earlier dispute was pending and claimed that the newer lease substantially covered the same disputed area. It called for the Minister of Mines, Steel and Solid Minerals Development and the Mining Cadastre Office to authenticate ML-129 and determine whether the lease is valid, subsisting and lawfully applicable to the Latya site.

The BYM also alleged inadequate host-community involvement in the process leading to the issuance or operation of ML-129, including questions concerning landowners' interests and Community Development Agreement requirements. It raised further concerns about the alleged deployment of Nigeria Police Force and Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps personnel to the mining site and called for clarification of who authorised the deployment and under what legal authority.

The association said it had also received reports of community members being arrested, detained or subjected to legal proceedings following complaints attributed to Mr. Egbagbe and called for independent investigation of those cases. It demanded the withdrawal of security personnel from the site within 24 hours unless supported by a valid court order or lawful directive, and said failure to receive a satisfactory government response within one week would lead it to pursue what it described as its constitutional right to peaceful assembly and lawful protest. The association simultaneously urged residents and youths in the affected communities to remain calm and law-abiding.

newsReports.lead_narrative: Finland's Ambassador to Nigeria, Sanna Selin, visited the Lagos State Ministry of Commerce, Cooperatives, Trade and Investment to explore potential areas of bilateral trade, investment and industrial cooperation with the state.

story_body: The Ambassador was received by the Commissioner for Commerce, Cooperatives, Trade and Investment, Folashade Ambrose-Medebem, who outlined the ministry's mandate and highlighted initiatives including the Lagos State Export Readiness Programme and the Lagos State Industrial Policy 2025–2030.

The engagement therefore focused on possible areas for practical cooperation spanning industrial modernisation, trade facilitation, digitalisation, maritime technology, sustainable mobility, creative industries and green innovation. newsReports.lead_narrative: Kwara State Governor Abdulrahman Abdulrazaq has announced an immediate ₦10 million government donation to residents affected by recent flooding in communities within Lafiagi Emirate and directed the State Emergency Management Agency to document the losses.
newsReports.editorial_notice: This News Report provides qualitative subnational coverage. Developing events in this narrative maintain visibility across tracked jurisdictions and do not alter current Policy Signal Index (PSI) standings.
story_body: The governor said he visited Lafiagi Emirate on October 1, 2026, to commiserate with residents affected by flooding in Pututa, Tswako, Likpata, Godangi and Ekko communities. He described the situation as saddening while outlining the immediate response by the state government.

According to the governor's statement, the government has donated ₦10 million for immediate support to residents affected by the natural disaster. He also directed the State Emergency Management Agency to take an inventory of losses as a basis for support to victims.

The governor said the state would continue working with relevant federal institutions and other stakeholders on a longer-term response to the flooding challenge. He identified the dredging of the River Niger as what the state considers a possible lasting solution to the flood problem.

During the visit, the governor also donated a new coaster bus to the College of Education Technical Lafiagi to support mobility at the institution. He additionally inspected ongoing reconstruction work at the Lafiagi Stadium.

The immediate response reported by the state therefore combines emergency financial assistance and loss assessment for affected communities with continued engagement on a longer-term response to flooding. The source did not provide a quantified assessment of the total flood damage.
